lead: Heart disease is a leading indirect cause of maternal death. Cardiac output rises by 40% and a diseased heart cannot meet the load. Rheumatic heart disease is the commonest cause locally and mitral stenosis the commonest lesion.
f: Cardiac output +40%, blood volume +40–50%, resistance falls · Three danger times: 24–32 wk (plateau), labour (each contraction adds 300–500 mL), and just after birth (autotransfusion: the highest load) · Normal: mild breathlessness, ankle oedema, bounding pulse, ejection systolic murmur, third sound · Investigate: orthopnoea, PND, haemoptysis, syncope, pulse over 100 or irregular, any diastolic murmur, raised JVP, basal crackles, cyanosis

sc: Cyanosis, loud P2, known VSD → Eisenmenger syndrome

f: Acquired: rheumatic heart disease, mitral stenosis, peripartum cardiomyopathy, IHD · Congenital: ASD, VSD, PDA; Fallot, Eisenmenger; coarctation; Marfan · NYHA I no symptoms · II moderate effort · III mild effort · IV at rest · Often worsens by one class as pregnancy advances

sc: Rheumatic history, mid-diastolic murmur, breathless at 28 wk → Mitral stenosis

f: Pulmonary hypertension and Eisenmenger (maternal death 40–60%) · Severe MS or AS · EF below 30% or NYHA III–IV · Previous peripartum cardiomyopathy with poor recovery · Marfan with aortic root over 4 cm · Advise against pregnancy; offer termination · Stenotic lesions are worse than regurgitant (fixed output)

Echocardiography is the key test (valve area, EF, pulmonary pressure, aortic root) · ECG, FBC (anaemia strains the heart), INR on warfarin · Maternal: heart failure and pulmonary oedema, AF and stroke, valve thrombosis, endocarditis, PPH, death · Fetal: FGR, preterm birth, stillbirth, congenital heart disease 3–5% if the mother has CHD, warfarin effects

sc: MS, 28 wk or just after birth, pink frothy sputum → Pulmonary oedema: sit up, furosemide

f: Joint team: cardiologist, obstetrician, anaesthetist · Repair the valve before pregnancy if needed; stop ACE inhibitors and statins · Clinic every 10–12 days; NYHA, pulse, lung bases each visit · Remove extra loads: treat anaemia, infection, hypertension, thyroid disease · Furosemide for congestion, beta-blocker (longer filling in MS), digoxin for AF, penicillin prophylaxis · Fetal echo at 20–22 wk if CHD; growth scans · Admit NYHA III–IV, AF or failure · Severe MS: balloon valvotomy in the second trimester · Mechanical valve: never stop anticoagulation; warfarin → LMWH at 6–12 wk

sc: MS, NYHA II, Hb 8 → Treat the anaemia first
MS with a new irregular pulse → AF: rate control + LMWH

f: Written plan by 36 wk; await spontaneous labour · Vaginal birth is safer; CS for obstetric reasons (or aortic root over 4 cm, failure) · Sit up or left lateral; restrict IV fluids, catheter · Early low-dose epidural (LMWH stopped 24 h before) · Shorten the second stage: forceps or ventouse · Third stage: oxytocin 5 IU slowly or low-dose infusion · PPH: oxytocin slowly, misoprostol; avoid carboprost · Endocarditis prophylaxis only for a prosthetic valve or previous endocarditis

tr: No ergometrine: it pushes blood into the heart and causes acute pulmonary oedema

f: HDU for at least 3 days: autotransfusion → pulmonary oedema in the first hours · Breathless with crackles: sit up, O₂, stop fluids, furosemide 40 mg IV · Restart LMWH 8–12 h after birth; mechanical valve → warfarin from day 5 · Breastfeeding safe · Contraception: progestogen-only (implant, injection, LNG-IUS); no combined pill; sterilisation if pregnancy is contraindicated

Heart failure from 32 wk of pregnancy to 6 months after birth, no other cause, EF below 45% · Risks: multiparity, twins, pre-eclampsia, age over 30, African women · Treat: furosemide, beta-blocker, hydralazine + nitrate (ACE inhibitor after birth), LMWH if EF below 35% · Half recover; recurs in the next pregnancy

sc: Breathless 2 months after birth, EF 30% → Peripartum cardiomyopathy
